title: Building Code application to a change of occupancy in an existing building
jurisdiction: British Columbia (specific local authority not named in published decision)

facts.text: An existing three-storey timber-frame barn was built in 2011 as an agricultural building under Part 9, with permit plans stating “not to be used for habitation – farm use only.” It was later used as a wedding assembly hall on the first storey and short-term residential use on upper storeys, with unsanctioned modifications.
The local authority requested a detailed professional analysis of deficiencies for assembly and residential uses and proposals to correct them; it found an initial code analysis inadequate.
The parties disputed how the existing-building provisions applied to the occupancy change.
